battleframe.setupWizard.title: BattleFrame Setup
battleframe.setupWizard.emptyTitle: No ruleset installed. That is a working BattleFrame.
battleframe.setupWizard.emptyBody: BattleFrame with no ruleset is a table and a ruler: scenes render, tokens move, and distance measures base-to-base in millimetres. What it has no opinion about is rules — turns, actions, and dice belong to a ruleset module, because no two games agree on them. Install a ruleset module and enable it, and it will appear here for you to choose. Until then, nothing is broken and nothing is missing.
battleframe.setupWizard.readyBody: Choose the ruleset that governs this world. Exactly one is primary; you can change it later from Settings.
battleframe.setupWizard.conflictWarning: Two ruleset modules both claim to be the primary ruleset for this world. BattleFrame will not activate either until you say which one governs — guessing would silently give you the wrong game.
battleframe.setupWizard.conflictInstruct: Set aside one ruleset's primary claim to resolve this now and pick the other. That lasts until the world reloads; to fix it for good, disable one of the modules in Manage Modules.
battleframe.settings.activeRulesetId.hin: The id of the ruleset module currently governing this world. Written by the setup wizard once a ruleset activates successfully.
battleframe.settings.setupCompleted.name: Setup Completed
battleframe.settings.setupCompleted.hint: Whether the setup wizard has been completed for this world. While false, the wizard opens automatically for the GM.
battleframe.settings.defaultGridUnit.hin: The unit label applied to new scenes. BattleFrame measures base-to-base regardless of this label; it only affects how distances are displayed.
battleframe.settings.setupWizardMenu.hin: Reopen the BattleFrame setup wizard to review installed rulesets or change which one is primary.
